findings: tests/possible-applications.test.js has 16 tests, and all 16 pass when run alone with `node --test`. The full suite (`node --test tests/*.test.js`) gives 177 pass and 1 fail. The one failure is `not ok 98 - S11: when reviewer-design has reviewed, it addresses and clears all four images against design/reference/`. That is the design v4 S11 failure the work order says to itemize as pre-existing and untouched. It is unrelated to this change, and no other test fails.

Spec scenarios S1 to S6 are each mapped to a named test. S7 is a run-report fact, and the test file's header comment says so. The mapped tests cover:
- the section id and its position after the FAQ and before the footer
- the kicker markup, title and introduction
- no imagery in the section
- four entries with identical attributes, two or three sentences each, comparable length, and no links, badges or emphasis
- exploratory markers (at least two in the diabetes entry, and a possible-future frame in its title or lead)
- glucose named only in the diabetes entry, and only in sentences that carry an exploratory marker
- absence of capability-claim shapes
- absence of insulin, treat, therapy, dose, diagnos, cure, manage-your-condition and delivery terms, plus extra groups for clinical and efficacy wording
- both footer sentences byte exact in the served page
- a src/page.js diff against base c55bc16 with zero deleted lines and no other production file changed
- a subsequence check that every base line of page.js survives in order
- the other routes still answering 200, and llms.txt free of glucose or diabetes
- the three R9 evidence checks

The assertions are real and not vacuous. Section, entry and diabetes lookups are asserted non-empty before use. Each forbidden-term group is a separate assertion with a named failure message. S3 also asserts that glucose is still named, so a section scrubbed of the application would fail.

Weakness, minor: the S6 evidence tests check the committed logs by regex and PNG headers, not by re-running the bundle or the browser. They confirm the evidence exists and has the right shape (wrangler command, exit 0, no-patch statement, zero console and page errors, a local Worker runtime, desktop-width PNGs of at least 20 KB that differ). They cannot prove the commands actually ran. The offline design accepts this, but the run verdict should rely on the evidence files themselves.
Weakness, minor: the S5 diff test hard-codes BASE = c55bc16 and fails with a clear message if that commit is missing from a shallow checkout. It passes here. CI needs full history for it.

The `erroring` guardrail regexes are broad. The `\bcontrol\w*` term in the efficacy group and `\bnew\b` in the badge check could flag harmless copy later. They are strict in the safe direction, and the current copy passes, so this is not a defect.

No test files were modified or removed. The only new tracked-candidate test file is tests/possible-applications.test.js, which fits R8. The evidence under evidence/possible-applications/ is already committed in 21786e4, because the S6 tests pass on a clean tree.
